# Masterpiece

> Masterpiece is a free, open-source (GPL-3.0) pipe organ sample player. It plays Hauptwerk-format, GrandOrgue and jOrgan sample sets, each with its own console, wiring, wind and swell boxes, on Windows, macOS, Linux, Raspberry Pi, Android, iPhone and iPad, as a standalone program and as VST3, LV2 and AU plugins. It is part of OpenPipes (openpipes.org), an open-source virtual pipe organ platform.

Key facts:

- Formats: Hauptwerk-format organ definitions (full, compact and composite) GrandOrgue organs (.organ definitions and .orgue packages) and jOrgan organs (.disposition files with their SoundFonts, sfArk included), opened from an unpacked folder or straight from their packages, including solid, multi-part and multi-volume RAR sets. Samples in WAV or WavPack at any rate.
- Composite organs: organs assembled from the pipework of several sample sets, each set read from its own archive.
- Split mode: the whole organ from a single keyboard, with up to three split points, a pedal bass from the left hand and a solo melody from the right.
- Installing: an organ installer that installs packages into an organs folder, upgrades them component by component and uninstalls them; favourites and the installed organs in one Open window; a Test Sound organ generated at the first start.
- Score player: MusicXML scores played through the organ, with repeats, endings, D.C., D.S. and Coda, ornaments, a tempo of your own, staves left silent for practice, and registration marks on the notes.
- Tuner: the pitch of a held key against the temperament, with its harmonics.
- Engine: custom AVX2, SSE2 and NEON vector code, 3 to 5 times the rendering speed with AVX2 at 512 voices; 725 voices per processor thread by default, up to 16,384.
- Memory: samples held compressed, lossless, with release tails streamed from disk. Our 44-stop reference sample set takes 16.2 GB at 24 bits as recorded, 5.39 GB compressed (3.0x less) and 3.62 GB compressed with releases streamed (4.5x less), bit for bit.
- Control: a MIDI channel per manual, MIDI learn for every stop, piston and swell shoe (SysEx included), generals, divisionals and a 999-frame stepper, temperaments, pitch and a transposer. A player crescendo of 32 steps on organs that have none, GrandOrgue sets among them. Tabs learned one after another, and console profiles that map a new organ by its stop names.
- Outputs: up to 64, each on device channels of its own, with sends, a room, an EQ and a crossover for subwoofers and speakers of several ways; a mixer with faders for outputs, divisions, perspectives and mixes of ranks.
- Tested with more than 100 organs, among them sets by Piotr Grabowski and Augustine's Virtual Organs.

## Links

- [Home page](https://masterpieceorgan.com/): features, figures, sound demos and a gallery of consoles
- [Downloads](https://masterpieceorgan.com/#platforms): the latest release for every system
- [Manual](https://masterpieceorgan.com/docs/): installing, opening sample sets, MIDI, audio, memory and streaming, every setting, and the developer guide
- [Latest release notes](https://github.com/bonninr/masterpiece/releases/latest)
- [Source code](https://github.com/bonninr/masterpiece): C++20 and JUCE
- [Questions and discussions](https://github.com/bonninr/masterpiece/discussions)
- [OpenPipes](https://openpipes.org): OpenPipes OS, Pipe2C hardware modules, console plans and the Organ Designer
